challenges.evidence: Vercel's October 14 report disclosed a Linux-kernel flaw capable of breaking sandbox isolation, demonstrated on researcher-controlled machines matching Vercel Sandbox's configuration. Vercel said it coordinated mitigation with the researcher and AWS; fixes were under private review and CVEs pending as of that report. No reports showed access to customer data. This is not evidence of a production breach or confirmation that the issue remains unresolved today.
challenges.challenge: Hardening Sandbox isolation against kernel-level vulnerabilities.

challenges.evidence: On September 7, a customer alleged unexpected automatic Vercel Agent charges, an unanswered billing case, and disabled production deployments. In a September 24 reply, Vercel said support had issued a refund the previous week. This is an individual, subsequently refunded complaint—not evidence of a platform-wide or still-unresolved problem.
challenges.challenge: Billing clarity and timely support escalation for automated Agent usage.

recent_changes.summary: BYOC keeps application compute and data within the customer's AWS boundary. Enterprise-Managed Authorization lets agents access connected services on employees' behalf through the organization's identity provider.

priorities.evidence: Vercel launched Drives into general availability, allowing agent workspaces, file-based memory, datasets, and build artifacts to persist across Sandbox runs.
priorities.priority: Make agent workloads persistent across runs.

priorities.priority: Expand enterprise adoption through centralized governance, identity controls, and customer-cloud deployment.

priorities.evidence: Vercel Shop became generally available with machine-readable product pages and agent shopping tools, extending the Shopify partnership beyond storefronts designed solely for people.
Vercel's Sandbox security report describes collaboration with researchers, AWS, and Trail of Bits, implementation of structural hardening recommendations, and work on kernel-vulnerability mitigation.
In a September 15 interview report, COO Jeanne DeWitt Grosser described extensive inbound sales-development automation and a home-built support agent handling most support cases.
priorities.priority: Automate internal go-to-market and support workflows with AI agents.

citations.title: Vercel Drives is now generally available
excerpts: **Published:** October 15, 2026 | **Authors:** Tom Lienard, Marc Codina Segura, Andy Waller, Luke Phillips\-Sheard, Joe Haddad
Vercel Drives is now generally available

A Drive is persistent storage that you mount as a directory in a Vercel Sandbox. Its files remain available after the sandbox stops, so later runs and other sandboxes can access them by mounting the same Drive. Use Drives to preserve an agent’s workspace or file-based memory across runs, or to make datasets, models, dependencies, and build artifacts available across sandboxes.

basis.reasoning: The changelog provides the launch date, availability status, and persistent-storage behavior.

citations.title: Findings from the $1M Vercel Sandbox challenge
excerpts: **Published:** October 14, 2026 | **Authors:** Andy Riancho
Immediately after being notified, we collaborated with the researcher to understand and mitigate the vulnerability

On top of that foundation, they gave us three structural recommendations, which we implemented: **Find and eliminate all trust in the guest.** Our control plane accepted values returned by software running inside the microVM, and every one of those values is tenant input. Anything that crosses the boundary should be derived server-side or signed with a key the guest cannot reach. **One policy, one decider.** Egress enforcement was split across subsystems that each parsed the same network policy independently, and they did not always agree. We now use one canonicalization routine per data type, one component per decision, and revalidate connections when policy changes. **Assume the next zero day.** Keep host and guest kernels up to date, reduce the kernel attack surface via build and runtime configs, disable nested virtualization, and use Firecracker’s jailer to run each microVM process with restricted permissions and isolate it from the rest of the host.

basis.reasoning: The report describes actual security collaboration and implemented structural hardening, supporting the security-investment priority.
